scope.quote: When fulfilling a redeem request, there are no checks to ensure that $\text{totalAssets()}$ is greater than the amount being fulfilled for the redemption. This omission will lead to an incorrect share calculation and to griefing (DoS) for users when they try to withdraw. I will describe the issue clearly below:

In the above function, if the current asset balance of this contract is less than the sum of $\text{totalPendingDepositAssets}$ + $\text{totalClaimableRedeemAssets}$ + $\text{totalCancelDepositAssets}$, $\text{totalAssets()}$ will return zero.

Now, if we call $\text{totalAssets()}$, it will return zero because the $\text{current\_balance}$ ($10\_000$) minus the reserved amount ($\text{totalClaimableRedeemAssets}$ of $1\_00\_000$) is less than zero. $\text{totalClaimableRedeemShares}$ will return $1\_00\_000$ (referencing the updated state after $\text{fulfillRedeemRequest}$, which is explained above).

Now, since the new user is depositing $1\_00\_000$, the number of shares the user will get is calculated as: $\mathbf{1\_00\_000 \times 10\_000 / 1\_00\_000}$, which is $\mathbf{10\_000}$ shares. This is incorrect, as the user should have received $1\_00\_000$ shares at the proper price. The magnitude of the loss depends on deposit amounts other than the fulfilled redemption. Since there is another $10\_000$ deposit by User 2, the circulating supply is $10\_000$; if there were no other users, it would be zero.
In the same way, if User 1 tries to withdraw before someone deposits 1_00_000, User 1's transaction will revert due to insufficient funds.
This will lead to share price manipulation and griefing ($\text{DoS}$) for users.
